questions.text: Do you work, or are you a student?
questions.say: Good morning. My name is Daniel, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about work or studies. Do you work, or are you a student?

cueCard.topic: Describe a useful skill that you have learned.
points: when and how you learned it
cueCard.explain: and explain why this skill is useful to you.

questions.text: Describe a useful skill that you have learned.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a useful skill that you have learned. You should say: what the skill is; when and how you learned it; how often you use it; and explain why this skill is useful to you.
Thank you. Was it difficult to learn?

questions.text: What skills do you think every young person should learn?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a useful skill you have learned. Now I'd like to ask you some more general questions about learning. What skills do you think every young person should learn?

questions.text: Do you think practical skills are taught well in schools today?
questions.say: Do you think practical skills are taught well in schools today?

questions.text: Is it easier to learn new things when you are young or when you are older? Why?
questions.say: Is it easier to learn new things when you are young or when you are older? Why?

questions.text: Many people now learn skills from online videos. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this?

questions.text: Which skills do you think will be most important for jobs in the future?
